title: Completed pullback completion unit is invertible in the strict reduction tower
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ a finitely generated ideal with $A/I$ additive torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ finite and perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes. For $W=T,T'$ use the small pro-etale site, the constant ring sheaves $\underline A_W$ and $\underline{P_n}_W$, module sheaves and the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(W,A)$ of $\underline A_W$-modules [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; module inverse image $g^*$ along the canonical identification $g^{-1}\underline A_T=\underline A_{T'}$ is exact and computes $Lg^*$. Put $\mathcal T_W=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_W))$ [def-weil-inverse-system], regarded as modules on the diagram site [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], with derived category $D(\mathcal T_W)$, constant-tower functor $\Delta$, and termwise inverse image $G_g:D(\mathcal T_T)\to D(\mathcal T_{T'})$ (exact). Let $\mathcal R_W(N)=\Delta N\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_W}(\underline{P_n}_W)_n$; for a flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to N$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] it is represented by the strict quotient tower $(Q\otimes_A\underline{P_n}_W)_n$. Let $C_W$ be derived completion with unit $\eta_N:N\to C_WN$, $C_WN=R\lim_n(N\otimes^L_A\underline{P_n}_W)$ [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction].

(i) For every $N\in D(T',A)$ the morphism $\mathcal R_{T'}(\eta_N):\mathcal R_{T'}(N)\to\mathcal R_{T'}(C_{T'}N)$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal T_{T'})$. At level $n$ its inverse is the map $(C_{T'}N)\otimes^L_A\underline{P_n}\to N\otimes^L_A\underline{P_n}$ adjoint, under extension of scalars to $\underline{P_n}$, to the $n$-th limit projection $C_{T'}N\to N\otimes^L_A\underline{P_n}$.

(ii) For every $K\in D(T,A)$, the termwise canonical isomorphisms $g^*(Q\otimes_A\underline{P_n}_T)\cong g^*Q\otimes_A\underline{P_n}_{T'}$ on a flat-term K-flat representative $Q$ of $K$ define a natural isomorphism $\tau_{g,K}:\mathcal R_{T'}(Lg^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_g\mathcal R_T(K)$ in $D(\mathcal T_{T'})$, independent of $Q$. Hence
$$q_{g,K}=\tau_{g,K}\circ\mathcal R_{T'}(\eta_{Lg^*K})^{-1}:\mathcal R_{T'}(C_{T'}Lg^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_g\mathcal R_T(K)$$
is a natural isomorphism of derived strict towers, compatible with every quotient transition.

(iii) If $K$ is derived $I$-complete, regard completed inverse image in the constant-coefficient categories as $C_{T'}Lg^*K$, the left adjoint of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] (Stacks 099N(2)). Put $M=Lg^*K$ and $H=G_g\mathcal R_T(K)$. The presentation in Stacks 099N(5) has comparison $R\lim(\tau_{g,K}):C_{T'}M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim H$. Define $\alpha^{\mathrm{const}}_{g,K,n}:(C_{T'}M)\otimes^L_A\underline{P_n}_{T'}\to g^*(K\otimes^L_A\underline{P_n}_T)$ in the finite coefficient derived category to be the scalar-extension adjunct of the composite $C_{T'}M\xrightarrow{R\lim(\tau_{g,K})}R\lim H\xrightarrow{p_n}H_n$, followed by the canonical finite-coefficient target comparison. Through the finite-evaluation and restriction-of-scalars comparisons, the level-$n$ component of $q_{g,K}$ equals $\alpha^{\mathrm{const}}_{g,K,n}$; in particular this projection-induced map is an isomorphism. All objects and maps here have constant coefficients; no completed-ring coefficient presentation or its additional coefficient-datum hypotheses are invoked.

proof.text: For inverse_finiteLimits, the down and up functors of AsSmall are equivalences and preserve finite limits. Composing with the pro-etale base-change functor proves finite-limit preservation on the small site. Its representable flatness gives Mathlib finite-limit preservation for the abstract sheaf pullback, and the named comparison transfers it to the constructed sheaf pullback used here.

Construct the underlying ring comparison from the canonical forgetful sheaf-pullback isomorphism and its adjunction-unit equation. Its inverse is the set-adjoint of the ring unit. Apply the unit-normalized underlying module inverse-image theorem to the resulting ring presentation, commute abelian inverse image with forgetting to sets, and bridge constructed and abstract sheaf pullbacks by uniqueness of left adjoints. Binary and nullary operation graphs are preserved because the transposed ring and module units preserve addition, multiplication, zero, one, and scalar multiplication. Ring naturality is the transpose of naturality of the ring adjunction unit. Identify the constant comparison with the canonical constant-section map using the constant-sheaf adjunction on a transported terminal object. These data give canonicalInverseImageData_existsUnique; its predicate fixes every data field, so adjunction injectivity, natural-transformation extensionality, and proof irrelevance give uniqueness.

old_proof.text: Model of $\mathcal R_W$. Let $Q\to N$ be a flat-term K-flat resolution [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] module sheaves on the diagram site are towers; every covering family of that site lies in a single level, so sections, sheafification and hence the sheaf tensor product over $\Delta\underline A_W$ are computed levelwise, and by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] kernels, cokernels and cohomology of tower complexes are levelwise. Hence $\Delta Q\to\Delta N$ is a quasi-isomorphism, every $\Delta Q^i$ is flat, and $\Delta Q$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]: for an acyclic tower complex $F$, level $n$ of $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes\Delta Q)$ is $\operatorname{Tot}(F_n\otimes_{\underline A_W}Q)$, acyclic because $F_n$ is acyclic and $Q$ is K-flat. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] (2) for the ring map $\Delta\underline A_W\to(\underline{P_n}_W)_n$ of the diagram site, $\mathcal R_W(N)$ is represented by $\Delta Q\otimes_{\Delta\underline A_W}(\underline{P_n}_W)_n=(Q\otimes_A\underline{P_n}_W)_n$ with transitions $1_Q\otimes\rho_n$. A morphism $N\to N'$ is a roof of chain maps between such resolutions (resolve its apex again by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]) and goes to the levelwise tensored roof. Thus evaluation at $n$ of $\mathcal R_W$ is naturally $F_n=-\otimes^L_A\underline{P_n}_W$, regarded over $\underline A_W$ by restriction of scalars, as asserted in the statement.

old_proof.text: Fix $N\in D(T',A)$, write $F_n=-\otimes^L_A\underline{P_n}$, and take $Q\to N$ as in Step 1. By [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction], $C_{T'}N$ is computed by a K-injective tower resolution $j:(Q\otimes_A\underline{P_m})_m\to J_\bullet$ followed by $\lim_mJ_m$; this is the model of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], whose evaluations $p_n:\lim_mJ_m\to J_n\cong F_nN$ are the limit projections. Its completion unit $\eta_N$ is the canonical map $N\to R\lim_m(N\otimes^L_A\underline{P_m})$, which [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] (last paragraph, with $\mathcal O=\underline A$) identifies with the derived-completion unit, respecting units. That canonical map is $Q\to\lim_mJ_m$ obtained by factoring the compatible maps $j_m\circ(x\mapsto x\otimes1):Q\to J_m$ through the limit, so $p_n\eta_N=u_{n,N}$, where $u_{n,N}:N\to\operatorname{Res}F_nN$ is the scalar-extension unit. Nothing here uses the cone model of the completion map; all limits are in the K-injective model. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction] on $T'$ with $\Lambda=A$ and $K=N$. Its hypotheses are exactly our Noetherian, additive-torsion and perfect-quotient assumptions; it imposes no completeness hypothesis on $N$, and its $L$ and $p_a$ are the same K-injective model. It gives an isomorphism $b_{n,N}:F_nC_{T'}N\to F_nN$, namely the scalar-extension adjoint of $p_n$. Naturality of this adjunction in the source identifies $b_{n,N}F_n(\eta_N)$ with the adjoint of $p_n\eta_N=u_{n,N}$, hence with $\mathrm{id}_{F_nN}$. Since $b_{n,N}$ is invertible, $F_n(\eta_N)=b_{n,N}^{-1}$. This proves the specified formula for the level-$n$ inverse.

old_proof.text: The morphism $f=\mathcal R_{T'}(\eta_N)$ already exists in the derived category of strict towers, since $\mathcal R$ is the functor in the statement. Evaluation of its K-flat quotient model is $F_n(\eta_N)$, which Step 2 proves invertible. By [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], kernels and cokernels in the tower category are levelwise. Thus the cohomology tower of a representative of $\operatorname{Cone}(f)$ evaluates to $H^i(\operatorname{Cone}(F_n\eta_N))=0$ at every $n$, and is itself zero. Its representative is acyclic; the map from zero to it is therefore a quasi-isomorphism, inverted in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The cone is zero and $f$ is invertible. This proves (i) in $D(\mathcal T_{T'})$, rather than constructing a morphism from a family of maps in $D(T',A)$. Evaluation of the unique inverse of $f$ is the inverse of its evaluation, so it is precisely $b_{n,N}$.

Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $Q$ of $K$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], $g^*Q$ is again flat-term K-flat. The normalized tensor comparison supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison-construction], with its data spelled out in [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison], gives chain isomorphisms $\beta_{n,Q}:g^*(Q\otimes_A\underline{P_n}_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*Q\otimes_A\underline{P_n}_{T'}$. For $\rho_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$, naturality in the second tensor factor gives the chain equation $\beta_{n,Q}\,g^*(1_Q\otimes\rho_n)=(1_{g^*Q}\otimes\rho_n)\,\beta_{n+1,Q}$. Naturality in the first factor gives the same commuting square for each chain map $Q\to Q'$, and the chain maps respect differentials. Hence $\beta_Q$ is a natural isomorphism of actual tower complexes, not just of their levelwise derived images. Its inverse has the orientation of $\tau_{g,K}$.

old_proof.text: If $s:Q\to Q'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between the chosen K-flat complexes, [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] (1) makes every $s\otimes\underline{P_n}$ a quasi-isomorphism. Levelwise exactness from [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] then makes the map of entire quotient towers a quasi-isomorphism. Exactness of constant-coefficient $g^*$, assumed in the statement, preserves these quasi-isomorphisms; applying the same change-of-rings assertion to $g^*s$ handles the other side. The constructions also respect chain homotopies: tensoring the homotopy with $1$ and then applying $g^*$ gives its homotopy at all levels, commuting with every $\rho_n$. The equivalence $W^{-1}\mathcal P\simeq D(T,A)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] now descends the natural strict isomorphism $\beta_Q^{-1}$ of Step 4. Indeed its naturality square holds for chain maps, hence for inverses of the quasi-isomorphisms just inverted, and hence for every composite in the localization. The descended $\tau_{g,K}$ is natural on the derived category and independent of the representative $Q$. This proves the first assertion of (ii).

For a morphism $a:M\to M'$, naturality of $\eta$ gives $\mathcal R(Ca)\mathcal R(\eta_M)=\mathcal R(\eta_{M'})\mathcal R(a)$; multiplying by the two inverses yields $\mathcal R(a)\mathcal R(\eta_M)^{-1}=\mathcal R(\eta_{M'})^{-1}\mathcal R(Ca)$. Combined with naturality of $\tau$, this is naturality of $q$. Both factors are morphisms in the derived category of strict towers, so their composite has that typing. More explicitly, if $t_n^N$ denotes the quotient transition on $\mathcal R(N)$, the transition equation for $f=\mathcal R(\eta_M)$ gives $t_n^M b_{n+1,M}=b_{n,M}t_n^{CM}$ after multiplication by the evaluated inverses. old_proof.text: Suppose $K$ is derived $I$-complete. The equivalence, finite-reduction maps and unit compatibility of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], together with [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], identify $C_{T'}Lg^*K$ with the completed pullback and identify its defining strict tower with $G_g\mathcal R_T(K)$ through $\tau_{g,K}$. Under these identifications its limit projection is $\tau_{g,K,n}p_{n,M}$. Step 2 says $b_{n,M}$ is adjoint to $p_{n,M}$; naturality of the same scalar-extension adjunction says $\tau_{g,K,n}b_{n,M}$ is adjoint to $\tau_{g,K,n}p_{n,M}$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction], $\alpha_n$ is exactly the map induced by that defining limit projection. Hence $q_{g,K,n}=\tau_{g,K,n}b_{n,M}=\alpha_n$ in the finite coefficient derived category, and also after restriction to constant $A$ coefficients. This compares the normalized maps, not merely the isomorphism classes of their endpoints, and proves (iii).
